newsitem.title: UK: BA welcomes report of open slot trading.
newsitem.headline: BA welcomes report of open slot trading.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday it welcomed the prospect of European backing for the legalised, commercial trade of airport take-off and landing slots.
"All I can say is we have been campaigning for such a move for some time and would warmly welcome a more open, transparent trading of slots," public relations manager Michael Blunt said.

The Commission said earlier in Brussels that plans under discussion within the EU executive, if adopted, would leave intact an existing twice-yearly share-out of new or unused slots at airports and legalise the so-called "grey" secondary market for airlines wishing to sell the slots they already have.

"This way of (secondary) trading works in the United States to very good effect, and it is only a matter of time before it becomes the norm in Europe," BA's Blunt said. "It will make the whole issue of trading more open and much more responsive."

His comments echoed those of a Commission official who told reporters: "The way we would like to proceed is to tighten up safeguards in the primary market and, where there is a secondary market, to make that absolutely transparent."
It would also clear up the current grey market which the EC fears can benefit bigger airlines by allowing them to build up dominant positions unofficially.

British Airways would not be drawn on the possible implications for its controversial plans for a transAtlantic alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines but Blunt said BA welcomed any easing of systems that slowed competition.

BA and American's alliance plan has been slammed by rivals and industry critics who claim the pair's dominance of slots at London's crowded and popular Heathrow Airport, especially at peak times for transAtlantic flights, is a competitive threat.
This week Britain's Office of Fair Trading completed a three-month study into the competition aspects of the proposed deal, passing its recommendations on to the trade ministry.
Industry observers predict that if the government does approve the alliance it will add conditions that insist on some reduction in the pair's share of Heathrow capacity.
Thus, commercial slot trading could be very timely for BA, and could assist the deal because, as one industry observer said, "it would seem to remove all obstacles to new entrants".
Charterhouse Tilney analyst Mike Stoddard said a legalised slot trade should boost the alliance plan's chances of success.
"This would be seen as a positive factor for BA. It would help smooth through the American deal it rights became transferrable for cash," he said.

Another analyst, James Halstead at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said BA's balance sheet could be improved by between 2.5 and 5.0 billion pounds ($3.9 to $7.83 billion), if the value of its Heathrow slot holdings could be included.
By 1200 GMT, BA's share price was up 13-1/2 pence at 575 pence, with dealers saying the slot news was the main driver. The rest of the London market was broadly lower on the day.
